title: MoteNN: Memory Optimization via Fine-grained Scheduling for Deep Neural Networks on Tiny Devices
problem: Deploying DNNs on tiny devices faces a fundamental contradiction between DNNs' substantial memory requirements and the stringent memory constraints of resource-limited devices. Prior works either incur significant latency overhead or use coarse-grained scheduling that limits memory reduction for complex networks.
motivation: Deploying DNNs on tiny edge devices is increasingly important but severely constrained by memory limitations, making efficient memory optimization critical.
method: MoteNN reduces peak memory by breaking neural networks into smaller pieces (called operators) and carefully scheduling when they run—since operations don't all need to be in memory at once, this cuts peak memory use overall. It introduces an Axis Connecting Graph (ACG), a graph structure that helps find the optimal way to partition and reschedule operations by focusing on memory bottlenecks, the parts of the network where memory is used up fastest. This achieves substantial memory reduction while keeping computation time nearly unchanged.
key_novelty: The Axis Connecting Graph (ACG) is a graph representation that enables fine-grained operator partitioning—splitting neural networks into smaller, optimally-scheduled pieces—to reduce peak memory while keeping computation time nearly the same.
contributions: Fine-grained operator partitioning approach for arbitrary DNN architectures
Axis Connecting Graph (ACG) representation for efficient graph-level partitioning
80% peak memory reduction with minimal latency overhead on tiny devices
primary_theme: Fine-grained scheduling for memory-efficient DNN deployment on edge devices
